title: Positive earnings surprise on stock returns

llm_response.content:
## 1. Identification Strategy  
Causal method: Event-study methodology (market-model abnormal returns).  

Why: We want the causal effect of a specific, precisely-timed information shock (a positive earnings surprise) on short-horizon stock returns.  The event-study compares realised returns in a narrow window around the announcement with a firm-specific counterfactual “normal” return predicted from a market model that is estimated on a pre-event estimation window.  

Key identifying assumptions  
• Market model validity: In the absence of the event, each firm’s return in the event window would follow the linear relation estimated in the [−10,−2] estimation window (ret = αᵢ + βᵢ·mkt_ret + ε).  
• No confounding news: No other firm-specific value-relevant events occur in [0,+2].  
• Efficient market / no anticipation: The earnings surprise is not leaked before day 0, so abnormal returns should cluster in [0,+2] only because of the surprise.  
• Cross-sectional independence (or mild correlation correctable with firm-level aggregation) so standard t-tests on firm-level CARs are valid.  

## 2. R Code
```r
# =======================================================
# Event study: positive earnings surprises
# =======================================================

# Load packages -------------------------------------------------------------
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(broom)
  library(readr)
})

# 1. Read data --------------------------------------------------------------
df <- read_csv("experiments/exp_b/data/s14_data.csv",
               col_types = cols(
                 stock_id = col_integer(),
                 event_day = col_integer(),
                 ret = col_double(),
                 mkt_ret = col_double(),
                 beta = col_double()
               ))

# 2. Estimate market model parameters (α_i , β_i) on [-10,-2] --------------
est_window  <- -10:-2

coefs <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% est_window) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  do({
    mod <- lm(ret ~ mkt_ret, data = .)
    tibble(alpha_hat = coef(mod)[1],
           beta_hat  = coef(mod)[2])
  })

# 3. Merge coefficients and compute abnormal returns -----------------------
df <- df %>% 
  left_join(coefs, by = "stock_id") %>% 
  mutate(AR = ret - (alpha_hat + beta_hat * mkt_ret))

# 4. Cumulative Abnormal Return (CAR) in [0,+2] -----------------------------
event_window <- 0:2

CAR_tbl <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_window) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

# 5. Test whether mean CAR > 0 ---------------------------------------------
mean_CAR <- mean(CAR_tbl$CAR)
t_res    <- t.test(CAR_tbl$CAR, mu = 0, alternative = "greater")

cat("============= MAIN RESULT =================\n")
cat("Mean CAR[0,+2] :", round(mean_CAR, 4), "\n")
cat("t-statistic    :", round(t_res$statistic, 2), "\n")
cat("p-value        :", signif(t_res$p.value, 4), "\n\n")

# 6. Robustness checks ------------------------------------------------------

## 6.1  Use supplied β (no α)  ---------------------------------------------
df <- df %>%
  mutate(AR_beta_given = ret - (beta * mkt_ret))

CAR_given <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_window) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR = sum(AR_beta_given, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

cat("Robustness 1: Using provided beta only\n")
print(t.test(CAR_given$CAR, mu = 0, alternative = "greater"))

## 6.2  Market-adjusted return (MAR)  ---------------------------------------
df <- df %>% 
  mutate(MAR = ret - mkt_ret)

CAR_MAR <- df %>% 
  filter(event_day %in% event_window) %>% 
  group_by(stock_id) %>% 
  summarise(CAR = sum(MAR, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop")

cat("\nRobustness 2: Market-adjusted returns\n")
print(t.test(CAR_MAR$CAR, mu = 0, alternative = "greater"))
```

## 3. Expected Findings  
Direction: Positive.  Positive earnings surprises are typically good news, so average abnormal returns in the immediate window should be significantly above zero.

Magnitude: For large-cap U.S. firms, typical announcement-window CARs after a positive surprise lie around +1% to +3%.  With 80 events, we expect a mean CAR ≈ +0.015 (1.5 %) and a t-statistic in the 3–5 range, easily rejecting the null of no abnormal return.

_ground_truth.identification_strategy: Event study — market model; positive surprise sample; event window [0,+2]
_ground_truth.conclusion_detail: Firms with positive earnings surprises earn significantly positive CAR
